previous.note: delivery was the only payment condition; no verifier parameter
sessions may write into the data set; live services

verification.note: Verified compute, deployed 2026-10-09. The ComputeService above accepts a verifier address on postJob; SP1ComputeVerifier below is one to pass.

sp1Verifier.checked: VERSION() read back from the deployed contract; contracts/test/RealProof.t.sol runs this same bytecode against a proof from our own guest, and against that proof with one byte changed.

sp1ComputeVerifier.note: IComputeProofVerifier adapter: refuses before looking at the proof unless its journal commits to the piece CIDs ComputeService derived for itself.

superseded.checked: SP1's own fixture proof from contracts/test/SP1VerifierGroth16.t.sol verifies here; the same proof with one byte changed is rejected.
superseded.why: superseded: v4.0.0-rc.3 cannot verify a v6.1.0 proof

superseded.note: IComputeProofVerifier adapter: checks the journal commits to the piece CIDs ComputeService derived, before asking SP1 whether the proof is good.
superseded.why: superseded: pointed at the old verifier

precompileProbe.note: Throwaway. Settles that FEVM implements modexp, ecAdd, ecMul and ecPairing, which a top-level eth_call cannot tell from a missing precompile — both return nothing.

note: Adds the opt-in verifier: a client may name a verifier contract when posting a job, and the price is released only if that verifier is satisfied as well as the delivery condition. Naming none behaves exactly as the previous deployment did.
